newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end mixed, speculatives dominate.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end mixed, speculatives dominate.

text.p: Stocks ended mixed with trading dominated by a slate of speculative issues, dealers and analysts said.
"The Second Board made a lot of gains. But we don't have too many foreigners and locals are slow" on the blue chips, said a dealer at K&N Kenanga.
The key Composite Index of large-capitalised stocks rose 0.69 of a point to 1,081.88. The Second Board of small-cap issues jumped 9.91 points or 1.75 percent to 576.08.
"Most of the day's activities were centered on second liners and speculatives," said G.K. Goh Stockbrokers in a commentary.
The stock of engineering firm Pilecon was boosted 58 cents to 4.66 ringgit, joining a group of other speculative issues, dealers said.
Current punting favourite MBf Capital, a financial services firm, retained the top-volume spot, gaining five cents to 5.20 on volume of 26.4 million shares traded.
Second boarders Seng Hup, Halim Mazmin, Esprit Group and Mercury advanced between 1.20 and 2.00 ringgit.
Among blue chips, Telekom gained 40 cents to 17.40 on thin volume of 252,000 shares with analysts giving mixed views on the reason for the rise.
